subject: share-revision-comparison
body:
## Description

Implement R1-R7 under shared-seven-character-revisions.
Preserve suite, reviewer, and gate results while giving the comparison rule one owner.

## Approach

Add orchestra/conductor/revision.py with the settled pure revision_matches function.
Route suite acceptance and suite checks, reviewer checks, and gate terms through it.
Preserve reviewer.revision_matches as a public import or re-export.
Remove duplicate private implementations without changing caller targets or prerequisites.
Do not put the rule in Canon record hashing.
Create tests/test_revision_policy.py with focused tests named r1_whitespace through r7_unrelated.
Use a common case matrix through public reviewer, suite, and acceptance checks.
Cover both prefix orders, seven versus six characters, normalized equality, and exact short equality.
Add a revision_gate_terms test through the real gate entry point using a disposable store.
Avoid Git object lookup, format validation, data migration, and unrelated gate repairs.
Run the affected tests and inspect old comparison names in imports and strings.
Own orchestra/conductor/revision.py, comparison wiring in suite.py, reviewer.py and gate.py, and tests/test_revision_policy.py.
title: Give Conductor revision comparison one owner

subject: shared-revision-policy
body:
## Requirements

R1: Revision comparison ignores surrounding whitespace.
R2: Revision comparison ignores letter case.
R3: Revision comparison rejects either empty normalized value.
R4: Revision comparison accepts identical nonempty normalized values.
R5: Revision comparison accepts a proper prefix when the shorter normalized value has at least seven characters.
R6: Revision comparison rejects a proper prefix when the shorter normalized value has fewer than seven characters.
R7: Revision comparison rejects different normalized values without a prefix relationship.
R8: The dashboard evidence label reports a Git revision match according to the shared revision rule.
R9: The dashboard evidence label does not classify a Canon sha256 record revision as a Git revision match.

## Acceptance criteria

Use one case matrix through the shared helper, the public reviewer gate, suite checks, acceptance-at-head checks, and dashboard evidence_panels.
Include full equality, seven-character prefixes, longer prefixes, six-character proper prefixes, unrelated values, empty values, whitespace, and mixed case.
Exercise prefix cases in both argument orders.
Include identical short nonempty values to distinguish equality from a proper prefix.
Verify the gate command's suite-at-head and acceptance-runner-at-head terms against the same policy.
Use disposable stores for stored checks and dashboard evidence records.
Verify dashboard output with a real temporary Git HEAD and a stored unsigned check.
Verify missing HEAD keeps the existing unknown display.
Verify Canon sha256 record revisions retain their existing display without a Git match claim.
Review imports to establish one owner of the comparison rule.
Run affected tests, required Python quality gates, the configured phase-end suite, and canon validate before implementation closure.

## Constraints

Preserve current suite and reviewer comparison results for valid string inputs.
Use one pure comparison function owned by Conductor.
Preserve reviewer.revision_matches as a public entry point.
Coordinate suite edits with fail-first-contracts.
Use temporary stores in tests.
Apply strict types without Any, cast, or new checker suppressions.

## Non-goals

Git object resolution, prefix uniqueness checks, revision format validation, and full-revision-only enforcement.
Record migration, historical evidence changes, new approval restrictions, and dashboard frontend changes.
Changes to suite phase identity, result selection, gate policy, reviewed-revision selection, or ancestry checks.
Changes to Canon record revisions or Tuner claim revision semantics.

## Invariants

Each selected caller uses the same comparison rule for the values it compares.
Callers retain ownership of their target revision and non-revision prerequisites.
Identical short nonempty values remain matches under the existing equality rule.
The dashboard comparison remains an evidence label, not permission to approve or sign.
Display shortening never determines comparison input.

## Assumptions

Inputs are strings supplied by existing callers.
Seven characters are a compatibility rule, not proof of Git object uniqueness.
The dashboard compares evidence with its repository HEAD.
Conductor gate terms can compare evidence with the reviewed revision.
Different comparison targets can produce different results without violating the shared rule.
